en: Udāna 5.8 Saṅghabhedasutta Thus have I heard—
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now on that occasion, on the Uposatha day, in the morning, the Venerable Ānanda dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Rājagaha for alms.
Devadatta saw the Venerable Ānanda walking for alms in Rājagaha.
Having seen him, he approached the Venerable Ānanda and said to him:
"Friend Ānanda, from this day forward, apart from the Blessed One and apart from the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, I shall perform the Uposatha and the formal acts of the Saṅgha.

Then the Venerable Ānanda, having walked for alms in Rājagaha and returned from his almsround after the meal, approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, this morning, having dressed and taken my bowl and robe, I entered Rājagaha for alms.
While I was walking for alms in Rājagaha, Venerable sir, Devadatta saw me.”
Having seen me, he approached me; having approached, he said this to me:
“From today forward, friend Ānanda, I shall perform the Uposatha and the formal acts of the Saṅgha apart from the Blessed One and apart from the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
Today, Bhante, Devadatta will split the Saṅgha and will perform the Uposatha and the formal acts of the Saṅgha.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Good is easily done by the good;
Good is difficult for the evil to do.”
“Evil is easily done by the evil;
evil is difficult for the noble ones to do.
